names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Πατερμούθιος, Κόπρις και Αλέξανδρος οι Οσιομάρτυρες», with the rank words left off.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 107, «Александр Египетский, воин, мч.», with the rank words after the first comma left off — «воин» is a rank the corpus’s `types` vocabulary carries as `soldier` and is therefore not part of the name. `fk.mjs` returns no other holder for «александр египетскии», the corpus’s other Alexanders of Egypt being `alexander-companion-of-agapius` and its twin, both stored as «Александр Египетский, Кесарийский (Палестинский)».

death.note: saint.gr dates the martyrdom by the reign and by the campaign: «αποκεφαλίστηκαν με διαταγή του Ιουλιανού του παραβάτη (361 - 363 μ.Χ.), όταν αυτός εκστράτευε κατά των Περσών». No year of birth is given and no year within the reign.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 июля ст. ст. — «Прмчч. Патермуфия , Коприя и мч. Александра (361-363).»

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, third name, and this folder’s man — name page 107, «Александр Египетский, воин, мч.», the SOLDIER who was standing by.  `alexander-17-december` IS A FOLDER THE DAY SCAN COULD NOT SEE: its only row is the Greek 17 December, so no held list for the menologion 9/7 names it, and it was found from `patermuthius-17-december`’s own `related`. The Serbian wave gave 9 July rows to the other two of the trio and not to him, because the Охридски пролог’s heading for the day names only Patermuthius and Coprius; this calendar names all three. The reading life4200 WAS OPENED and is one paragraph: Patermuthius and his disciple Coprius were Egyptian hermits whom the apostate emperor had brought before him and tried to turn to paganism, saying craftily that he too had once served Christ and had learned that only the pagan gods can save; Coprius was taken in by the emperor’s promises and denied Christ, but by his elder’s prayers and tearful admonitions came to know his fall, repented and confessed himself a Christian again; the emperor had him cruelly tortured while Patermuthius strengthened his brother’s courage and patience, and one of the soldiers, by name Alexander, seeing what Coprius suffered, believed in Christ and was sentenced to be burned, while Patermuthius and Coprius were beheaded. THAT IS THE SAME COMPANY, THE SAME REIGN AND THE SAME ORDER OF EVENTS saint.gr gave these three folders, and the line’s «(361-363)» is exactly the interval they already carry. `dates` UNCHANGED. The manner of each death — the sword for two, the fire for Alexander — is in this reading where saint.gr gave only the beheading of all three, and it is recorded here and in no field. The entry names the emperor and no place; «Египетский» on the name pages is the one geography and it is in the stored name forms. No hymn on the day page stands under any of the three names. The line grades him «мч.» apart from the other two’s «Прмчч.», which is the same distinction saint.gr makes in prose and which this folder’s `venerable-martyr` does not carry; `types` UNCHANGED and no `soldier` was added, the word «воин» standing on the name page and in this note and in no field.  THE DAY PRINTS TWO ENTRIES, EACH NAMING A PATERMUTHIUS AND A COPRIUS, AND THEY ARE FOUR DIFFERENT MEN WITH FOUR NAME PAGES. The third entry is «Прмчч. Патермуфия , Коприя и мч. Александра (361-363).», the venerable-martyrs under Julian the Apostate, name pages 1744, 1281 and 107; the fourth is «Прпп. Патермуфия и Коприя Египетских (V).», the venerables of the fifth century, name pages 1745 and 1280. Each page lists «День памяти: 9 июля» and no other day, and the two pairs have a reading each, life4200 and life4201, BOTH OPENED. The corpus’s own folders divide the same way: `patermuthius-17-december`, `copris-17-december` and `alexander-17-december` are the martyr trio off saint.gr’s 17 December, and `copres-the-egyptian` is the venerable off doxologia.ro’s and the Охридски пролог’s 9 July. Only the venerable Patermuthius had no folder, and he is the arrival. BECAUSE THE RANK IS WHAT THE CALENDAR USES TO TELL THE PAIRS APART, the stored forms collide once the ranks are stripped, and TWO `READ_FOLDS` KEYS were written in the same commit for the two two-holder folds. TWO ENTRIES OF THIS DAY WERE WITHHELD AND ARE NAMED IN THE REPORT, both folders already carrying a VENERATED russian row on another Julian day: `pancratius-of-tauromenium` on 9 февраля (three hymns on this page left uncopied) and `cyril-of-gortyna` on 6 сентября (two hymns left uncopied). BRIEF-RUSSIAN §4 forbids a draft on such a folder and BRIEF.md §4 sanctions a second-day note; the author has not ruled, so nothing was written for either.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Πατερμούθιος, Κόπρις και Αλέξανδρος οι Οσιομάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The entry enumerates its company — three named men — so it is a folder each, and each relates the other two.** The page's whole narrative is three sentences: Christians full of piety and zeal were tortured and at last beheaded by order of Julian the Transgressor, whose years it gives as 361 to 363, when he was campaigning against the Persians; Copris, a young man, lost his nerve a little at first, but Patermuthius strengthened him with his warm words; and all three underwent the martyr's death chanting hymns to Christ. It names no place at all, so no coordinate is proposed, and it prints no hymn. **The corpus already keeps a `patermuthius-the-martyr` and a `copris-of-palestine`, and neither is one of these: that Patermuthius is the nobleman who suffered on 17 Σεπτεμβρίου with Elias and the bishops Peleus and Nilus under the earlier persecution, and that Copris is a venerable of 24 Σεπτεμβρίου. Two entries on one calendar are two commemorations, and these three are under Julian.** The page carries two epigrams, one in which Copris cries to Patermuthius that he has been made sharer of his life and of his sword, and one which gives Alexander a double crown for ascesis and for the blade; nothing is drafted from them.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).
